title: Ventricularis delamination causing acute left main obstruction during TAVI: a case report.
authors: Bo Fu; Fenlong Xue; Xiquan Song; Qingliang Chen; Nan Jiang
abstract:
Acute coronary obstruction is a rare but potentially fatal complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), most commonly resulting from displacement of a calcified native leaflet. We describe an unusual mechanism involving delamination of native aortic leaflet tissue with subsequent coronary ostial obstruction.
An 80-year-old woman with severe symptomatic calcific aortic stenosis underwent transfemoral TAVI with a self-expanding valve. During valve deployment, she developed abrupt haemodynamic collapse with marked ST-segment elevation. Emergency angiography demonstrated acute left main coronary obstruction, while transoesophageal echocardiography revealed a newly developed mobile flap-like structure in the ascending aorta, raising concern for acute aortic dissection. Emergency surgical exploration excluded aortic dissection and demonstrated delamination of native aortic leaflet tissue, macroscopically considered to involve the ventricularis layer. The detached tissue had prolapsed into the left coronary ostium, causing mechanical obstruction of coronary inflow. Excision of the obstructing tissue and surgical aortic valve replacement restored coronary perfusion.
This case expands the mechanistic spectrum of TAVI-related coronary obstruction and highlights an important diagnostic pitfall. Native leaflet delamination may produce a mobile intra-aortic flap mimicking acute aortic dissection while simultaneously causing catastrophic coronary obstruction. Recognition of this rare mechanism may facilitate prompt diagnosis and appropriate rescue intervention.

title: A Novel Intraluminal Microtube Anastomosis System (IMAS) for Rapid Rat Microvascular Reconstruction: Development and Experimental Evaluation.
authors: Sam-Youl Yoon
abstract: Background/Objectives: Conventional interrupted microvascular anastomosis is technically demanding and time-consuming. We developed an intraluminal microtube anastomosis system (IMAS) in which circumferential anchoring ridges on the outer surface mechanically retain each arterial end while two external circumferential ligatures secure the reconstruction. This study compared IMAS with conventional interrupted microsurgical anastomosis in a rat infrarenal abdominal aortic model. Methods: Forty male Sprague Dawley rats (250-300 g) were allocated to IMAS (n = 20) or conventional interrupted microsurgical anastomosis (n = 20). Random-sequence generation and allocation concealment were handled by an animal-experiment assistant. All formal procedures were performed by the same surgeon, who was proficient in conventional microsuturing and had completed 10 pilot IMAS procedures before the study. Anastomosis time was measured from complete aortic transection to restoration of flow after clamp removal. Patency was assessed at 1 week and 1 month by color Doppler ultrasonography, with terminal gross examination at 1 month. The study was exploratory and was not powered as a patency non-inferiority or equivalence study. Results: Mean anastomosis time was 5 min 30 s ± 60 s with IMAS and 20 min 32 s ± 75 s with conventional suturing (p < 0.001). The between-group mean difference (conventional minus IMAS) was 902 s (95% CI, 859-945 s), corresponding to an approximately 73% reduction. Patency was 19/20 (95%) in both groups at 1 week (p = 1.000) and 18/20 (90%) in both groups at 1 month (p = 1.000). No gross device migration, aneurysmal dilatation, or anastomotic leakage was observed in patent IMAS-treated vessels at necropsy. Conclusions: In this exploratory rat model, IMAS substantially shortened reconstruction time. The observed short-term patency proportions were the same in the two groups, but the study was not sufficiently powered to establish equivalence or non-inferiority in patency. Histological response, lumen stenosis, quantitative flow, mechanical strength, material biocompatibility, and longer-term outcomes require further evaluation.

title: The Fate of Mitral Valve Regurgitation After TAVI.
authors: Karin Steiner; Melchior Burri; Nina Feirer; Tobias Rheude; Hendrik Ruge; Markus Krane; Keti Vitanova
abstract: Background: Outcomes of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) for severe aortic stenosis with concomitant severe mitral regurgitation (MR) remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to quantify the evolution of high-grade MR after TAVI, compare changes using MR etiology, and assess associations between MR etiology, early improvement, or residual discharge MR and mortality. Methods: In a retrospective single-center cohort, 112 TAVI patients with baseline more-than-moderate MR were included (functional n = 94; degenerative n = 18). MR grade was assessed pre-TAVI, at discharge, and at last available follow-up (serial studies up to ≥5 years), and 5-year all-cause mortality was analyzed. Results: At discharge, 34% of patients improved by more than one MR grade, and 26% by one grade. Among 45 patients with available late echocardiographic follow-up, 62% improved by more than one grade, 24% by one grade. Exploratory five-year survival analyses did not demonstrate a significant difference for MR etiology (p = 0.23), discharge MR grade (p = 0.11), or MR improvement status (p = 0.12). Conclusions: Among patients surviving to longitudinal echocardiographic follow-up, MR reduction was frequently observed after TAVI. Exploratory analyses did not demonstrate statistically significant differences in 5-year survival according to MR etiology, early MR improvement, or discharge MR severity. However, limited sample size and incomplete follow-up preclude definitive prognostic conclusions. Overall, these findings are compatible with a surveillance-first management, and with individualized consideration of adjunctive mitral therapy for persistent higher-grade symptomatic MR.

title: Self-Expanding Stent-Assisted Reconstruction of Distal Supra-Aortic Vessels in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A Comparative Analysis.
authors: Bowen Li; Feng Shi; Zhipeng Hu; Zongli Ren; Zhiyong Wu; Luocheng Li; Zhiwei Wang
abstract: Background: Supra-aortic vessel reconstruction during total aortic arch replacement in acute Stanford type A aortic dissection patients with dissected distal supra-aortic vessels remains technically challenging; proximal supra-aortic vessel replacement alone carries a high risk of neurological complications secondary to intimal inversion. This study aims to evaluate clinical outcomes of self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction compared with proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone. Methods and Results: We performed a single-center retrospective comparative analysis of 49 consecutive patients undergoing emergency total aortic arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection from January 2022 to December 2023. Patients were divided into two groups according to intraoperative anatomy and surgeon decision: self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction (SAVR, n = 26) and proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone (PRVA, n = 23). Neurological outcomes related to supra-aortic vessel intimal inversion, operative parameters, blood product transfusion, and short-term complications were analyzed. The mean follow-up was 18.2 ± 4.1 months (range, 12-24 months). The SAVR group exhibited significantly lower supra-aortic vessel stenosis rate (3.8% vs. 30.4%, p < 0.001) and zero cases of intimal inversion-related luminal collapse versus five cases in the PRVA group (0 vs. 5, p = 0.02). Numerically fewer cases of symptomatic stroke (0% vs. 8.7%, p = 0.09) and radiographic cerebral infarction (3.8% vs. 13.0%, p = 0.17) were observed in the SAVR group, though the differences did not achieve statistical significance. Red blood cell and fresh frozen plasma transfusion requirements, mechanical ventilation duration, and ICU stay length were significantly lower in the SAVR cohort. Cardiopulmonary bypass time and 30-day mortality were comparable between groups. Conclusions: Self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction represents a promising technical option during total arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection with distal supra-aortic dissection, associated with superior branch vessel patency and favorable numerical trends in neurological and recovery-related endpoints, with a comparable early-term safety profile. Potential benefits require further validation in larger cohorts.

title: Staged Management with Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in a Patient with ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis, and Recurrent Cardiogenic Shock: A Case Report.
authors: Zhongheng Li; Weili Teng; Ruining Li; Liyun He; Dan Li; Lincheng Yang; Mengsha Gao; Ling Xu; Yupeng Wang; Ming Cui; Lijie Sun
abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Cardiogenic shock after successful culprit-vessel revascularization may remain multifactorial when important structural heart disease coexists. Case Presentation: We report an 81-year-old man with extensive anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction, low-gradient calcific aortic stenosis (AS) with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, and cardiogenic shock. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention of a completely occluded proximal left anterior descending artery was performed under intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support. Echocardiography showed an aortic valve area of 0.53 cm2, a mean transvalvular gradient of 25 mmHg, and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 32%. Although the findings raised concern for a classical low-flow, low-gradient AS phenotype, the low-flow state and true-severe AS could not be formally confirmed because stroke-volume index, dobutamine stress echocardiography, and standardized CT calcium scoring were unavailable. After IABP removal on day 6, profound recurrent shock with lactic acidosis and multiorgan hypoperfusion developed on day 10. IABP reinsertion was followed by improvement in systemic perfusion, whereas brief trial-off periods reproduced hemodynamic and symptomatic deterioration. TAVR was performed on day 24 after recovery of end-organ function, discontinuation of vasoactive drugs, partial platelet recovery, and completion of CT-based procedural planning. IABP was removed the next day, and the patient was discharged on day 30 with an ejection fraction of 42%. Conclusions: Recurrent shock after successful culprit-vessel reperfusion should prompt reassessment for persistent structural hemodynamic burdens. Temporary support may serve as a bridge to recovery and individualized procedural planning in selected patients, but the observed improvement after TAVR represents a temporal association in a multifactorial shock state and should not be interpreted as evidence for routine IABP use in infarct-related cardiogenic shock or a predetermined delay before valve intervention.

title: Short- and Mid-Term Effects of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement on Heart Rate Variability in Patients With Aortic Valve Stenosis.
authors: Emre Pacaci; Abdullah Yildirim; Mert Evlice; Guluzar Tras; Cuma Suleymanoglu; Muhammet Salih Ates; Mukremin Coskun; Emre Sezici; Mustafa Ozan Gursoy; Omer Sen; Omer Genc; Ibrahim Halil Kurt
abstract:
Heart rate variability (HRV) reflects autonomic nervous system balance and has emerged as a potential prognostic marker in cardiovascular diseases. However, the relationship between HRV and mortality following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) remains unclear.
This prospective cohort study included 230 patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis who underwent TAVR between June 2022 and June 2024. Twenty-four-hour Holter electrocardiography recordings were obtained one day before and at 3 months after the procedure to assess HRV using both time- and frequency-domain parameters.
Among the 230 patients enrolled, the 12-month all-cause mortality rate was 14.3%. Among frequency-domain parameters, the pre-TAVR low frequency/high frequency (LF/HF) ratio improved markedly from 2.20±1.45 to 1.54±0.85 (p<0.001). In the time domain, standard deviation of NN intervals (89-103 ms, p=0.027), standard deviation of the averages of NN intervals (68-83 ms, p=0.003), and percentage of successive RR intervals (10.0%-12.0%, p=0.036) all showed significant improvements, while root mean square of successive RR interval differences remained unchanged. The pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio was significantly lower in survivors and provided the best discrimination for 1-year mortality prediction (area under the curve 0.815; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.750-0.881). Calibration analysis confirmed excellent predictive accuracy (C-index, 0.81; Brier score, 0.104; pseudo-R2, 0.285). Patients with a pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio>1.34 had significantly lower mortality at follow-up (hazard ratio [HR] 0.103; 95% CI 0.042-0.250; log-rank p<0.001), and this association remained significant in landmark analysis beyond 3 months (HR 0.163; log-rank p<0.001).
HRV parameters provide meaningful prognostic information in patients undergoing TAVR. Among them, a reduced pre-TAVR LF/HF ratio is independently associated with increased 1-year mortality and may serve as a practical, non-invasive marker for risk stratification.

title: Association Between Revascularization Timing and Outcomes for Coronary Artery Disease in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
authors: Masashi Yamaguchi; Futoshi Yamanaka; Koki Shishido; Noriaki Moriyama; Tomoki Ochiai; Hirokazu Miyashita; Yoichi Sugiyama; Daisuke Sato; Eiji Koyama; Kunihiko Shimizu; Kazuki Tobita; Takashi Matsumoto; Shingo Mizuno; Yutaka Tanaka; Masato Murakami; Shigeru Saito
abstract:
Coronary artery disease (CAD) is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS), yet the optimal timing of coronary revascularization in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain.
We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with severe AS and stable CAD, defined as fractional flow reserve ≤0.80, instantaneous wave-free ratio ≤ 0.89, or visual stenosis ≥90%, who underwent TAVI between October 2013 and July 2023. Patients were categorized into two groups: PCI-first and TAVI-first. The primary endpoint was 1-year incidence of major adverse cardiac events (MACE: all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, and unplanned revascularization). The secondary endpoint was 3-year MACE stratified by PCI after TAVI among the TAVI-first group.
Of 1126 TAVI patients, 209 met criteria for concomitant CAD (PCI-first, n = 112; TAVI-first, n = 97). The TAVI-first group had lower frailty and fewer New York Heart Association functional class III/IV symptoms, whereas the PCI-first group had more blood transfusions. At 1 year, the crude incidence of MACE was higher in the PCI-first group, although this difference was not significant after propensity score adjustment (HR 1.62; 95% CI 0.60-5.2; p = 0.36). Among TAVI-first group, patients who underwent PCI after TAVI had a lower incidence of MACE (log-rank p = 0.007), but the 90-day landmark analysis showed no significant difference (0/24 vs. 5/62 events; log-rank p = 0.23).
In patients with severe AS and CAD, a PCI-first strategy was associated with a higher incidence of bleeding and transfusion without improvement in short-term outcomes. A TAVI-first strategy with selective PCI during follow-up may be a reasonable alternative, although the long-term benefit of post-TAVI PCI awaits confirmation in randomized trials.

title: Task Force 4: Clinical Considerations for the Care of Athletes with Genetic Cardiomyopathies.
authors: Sabiha Gati; Michael J Ackerman; Aaron L Baggish; Jonathan H Kim; Benjamin D Levine; Martin Maron; Matthew Martinez; Sharlene M Day
journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
abstract: The updated AHA/ACC Scientific Statement on Clinical Considerations for Competitive Sports Participation for Athletes with Cardiovascular Conditions presents the clinical considerations for athletes with genetic cardiomyopathies, including hypertrophic, dilated, arrhythmogenic, and left ventricular hypertrabeculation. This ACSM Official Pronouncement complements the 2020 ACC/AHA Scientific Statement by providing athlete-specific context, practical guidance for shared decision-making, and genotype-informed risk assessment for competitive sports participation, moving away from blanket sports disqualifications. Sports participation recommendations for each condition are tailored to risk levels, symptomatology, and genotype. Regular follow-ups and close surveillance are advised. This evolving approach underscores the importance of individualized care, ongoing research, and the integration of new data to better inform shared decision-making on the risks and benefits of competitive sports in athletes with cardiomyopathies.

title: Preoperative Dependent Functional Status Is Associated with Worse 30-Day Pulmonary Complications in Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement: An Insight from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program Database From 2005-2021.
authors: Renxi Li; Deyanira J Prastein
abstract:
While current cardiac surgery risk scores do not account for preoperative functional status, it has been linked to adverse outcomes in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, in surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR), preoperative functional status remains underexplored.
To examine the impact of preoperative functional status on 30-day SAVR outcomes to provide insights into clinical decision-making and postoperative care. Methods: Patients undergoing SAVR were identified from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database from 2005 to 2021. A 1:3 propensity-score matching was applied to patients with dependent (DFS) and independent (IFS) functional status. Thirty-day outcomes were assessed.
After propensity-score matching, DFS and IFS patients showed similar mortality (11.11% vs. 9.42%, P = 0.39) and major adverse cardiovascular events (9.91% vs. 9.11%, P = 0.66). Patients with DFS had higher risks of pulmonary complications (29.43% vs. 21.64%, P < 0.01) including pneumonia (13.21% vs. 9.21%, P = 0.04) and prolonged mechanical ventilation over 48 hours (25.83% vs. 15.42%, P < 0.01) but lower bleeding requiring transfusion (51.65% vs. 67.49%, P < 0.01). DFS patients were more likely to be discharged not to home (71.52% vs. 47.75%, P < 0.01) and had longer operation time (315.2 ± 130.5 vs. 293.5 ± 119.8 min, P < 0.01) and LOS (18.47 ± 14.30 vs. 15.07 ± 12.83 days, P < 0.01).
While SAVR is relatively safe in eligible DFS patients considering its mortality and cardiac outcomes, it is imperative to emphasize preoperative functional status assessments and closely monitor postoperative pulmonary complications.

title: Aortic valve calcification and one-year paravalvular leak after transcatheter aortic valve replacement: limited role of asymmetry.
authors: Pragati Basera; Roya Anahita Mousavi; Chisom Enwere; Minel Soroa; Edgar Argulian; Leila Alizadeh; Marcos Ferrandez-Escarabajal; Carlo Mannina; Lakshay Chopra; Samin K Sharma; Annapoorna S Kini; Stamatios Lerakis
abstract:
Paravalvular leak (PVL) is a significant complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Although total aortic valve calcification (AVC) burden and self-expandable valves are predictors of PVL, the impact of leaflet-specific AVC asymmetry remains uncertain. The authors evaluated the association between AVC asymmetry and mild or greater PVL at 1 year after TAVR and its interaction with valve type.
Patients undergoing TAVR between January 2022 and May 2025 with preprocedural noncontrast cardiac computed tomography and 1-year transthoracic echocardiography were included. Asymmetric AVC was defined as greater than 50% of total AVC on a single cusp.
Among 530 patients (mean age, 79 ± 8 years; 45.5% female), 130 (24.5%) had mild or greater PVL at 1 year. Total AVC was higher in women (1747 vs 1125 AU; P less than .001) and men (2612 vs 2063 AU; P less than .001) with mild or greater PVL, with greater calcification across all cusps. AVC asymmetry was comparable between PVL and non-PVL groups (33.1% vs 41.4%; P = .093). Total AVC independently predicted PVL (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.036 per 100 AU; P < .001), whereas asymmetry did not (adjusted OR, 0.912; P = .681). No significant interaction occurred between valve type, AVC asymmetry, and PVL (P = .224).
Total AVC independently predicts mild or greater PVL at 1 year after TAVR, whereas leaflet-specific asymmetry and valve type provide no additional predictive value.

title: Left Bundle Branch Optimized Resynchronization Therapy for Persistent Ventricular Dysfunction After Complex PCI and TAVR.
authors: Esteban Yu Hern Chin; Keng Tat Koh; Asri Bin Said; Ing Xiang Pang; How Kiat Khor; Alan Yean Yip Fong; Tiong Kiam Ong; Yen Yee Oon
abstract:
Severe aortic stenosis with complex coronary artery disease presents challenges in patients unsuitable for surgery. Persistent left bundle branch block (LBBB) after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) may impair ventricular recovery.
A 67-year-old man underwent high-risk left main-left anterior descending percutaneous coronary intervention, complicated by cardiogenic shock and severe left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Subsequent TAVR achieved favorable valve hemodynamics but was followed by new-onset left bundle branch block and persistent LV dysfunction. Left bundle branch pacing achieved complete correction only at high output. A coronary sinus lead was added for left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy with a defibrillator (LOT-CRTD). At 3 months, LV function fully recovered with reverse remodeling and marked symptom improvement. Why Beyond the Guideline: Optimal percutaneous coronary intervention-TAVR timing and device strategies for post-TAVR LBBB with LV dysfunction remain poorly defined in current guidelines.
LOT-CRTD may provide effective cardiac resynchronization when isolated left bundle branch pacing cannot achieve optimal correction.
Sequence of PCI-TAVR remained individualized. LOT-CRT is a viable strategy to facilitate ventricular recovery for post-TAVR LBBB.

title: "Whiplash Motion" in Cardiac Intimal Sarcoma With Functional Mitral Stenosis and Dynamic LVOT Obstruction.
authors: Norikazu Oshiro; Takeshi Yoshida; Bunpachi Kakii; Takuya Higuchi; Shinichi Mitsuyama; Masato Furui; Haruo Suzuki; Takashi Kawashima; Shin-Ichi Nakatsuka; Yuki Kubo
abstract:
Cardiac intimal sarcoma (CIS) usually presents as an isolated left atrial mass; pan-left-heart involvement producing simultaneous inflow and outflow obstruction is rare.
A 43-year-old man presented in acute heart failure (B-type natriuretic peptide 948.8 pg/mL; right ventricular systolic pressure 59 mm Hg). Imaging showed a tumor in the left atrium and ventricle: an atrial mass infiltrated the mitral leaflet, causing functional mitral stenosis, whereas a mobile papillary-muscle component showed a "whiplash motion," prolapsing into the left ventricular outflow tract and protruding through the aortic valve in systole. Emergency debulking and mechanical mitral valve replacement followed; histopathology confirmed CIS (mouse double minute 2 homolog/cyclin-dependent kinase 4 positive, mouse double minute 2 homolog-amplified). Although adjuvant carbon-ion radiotherapy provided temporary control, the patient died 20 months later.
We propose the "whiplash motion" sign and highlight the trade-off between mechanical-valve durability and bleeding risk during thoracic radiotherapy.
CIS can cause dual left-heart obstruction through multicomponent tumor dynamics; prosthetic valve choice should anticipate multimodality oncologic management.

title: Extensive Native Aortic Valve Infiltration and Early Bioprosthetic Valve Degeneration in Low-Grade Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia.
authors: Kai Yi Wu; Imran Chaudhry; Russell W Sterrett; Gabor T Gyenes; Matthew F Church; D Ian Paterson; Brian H Sonnenberg
abstract:
Cardiac manifestations of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) are extremely rare, particularly involving valves.
A patient with low-grade CLL presented with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis. Following surgical aortic valve replacement, the patient experienced rapid degeneration of her surgical bioprosthetic aortic valve, necessitating valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Re-evaluation of her excised native aortic valve tissue on histology with immunohistochemical confirmation revealed extensive CLL infiltration.
Extensive CLL infiltration of the aortic valve is an extremely rare phenomenon. This case raises the hypothesis that a clonal lymphoproliferative process may contribute to calcific aortic stenosis and possibly early bioprosthetic structural valve deterioration. Additional studies are needed to further evaluate this association.
CLL can rarely affect cardiac valves and may contribute to the development of native valve stenosis. Additional studies are required to determine whether CLL is a risk factor for early prosthetic structural valve deterioration.

title: Concomitant Wire-Loop Repositioning and Transapical Valve Replacement for a Migrated Sutureless Aortic Valve.
authors: Yusuke Hamada; Takuji Kawamura; Daisuke Yoshioka; Yoshiki Watanabe; Yusuke Misumi; Ai Kawamura; Shin Yajima; Shunsuke Saito; Kazuo Shimamura; Shigeru Miyagawa
abstract:
Sutureless aortic prosthesis migration is rare but potentially catastrophic.
A 78-year-old woman on hemodialysis underwent minimally invasive double valve replacement using a sutureless aortic bioprosthesis. Failure to wean from cardiopulmonary bypass prompted intraoperative angiography, which raised suspicion of cranial migration of the aortic prosthesis, with bilateral coronary hypoperfusion; subsequent computed tomography confirmed the diagnosis. Because repositioning after surgical excision of the native leaflets would cause severe aortic regurgitation, a transapical transcatheter valve was prepositioned before transfemoral wire-loop repositioning. Coronary flow was restored, the failed valve was replaced, and 5-month follow-up showed preserved ventricular function and stable frame position.
Prepositioning a transapical transcatheter valve before wire-loop repositioning enabled immediate valve replacement while minimizing the empty-annulus interval.
Failed passage of a Perceval sizer should preclude sutureless implantation; prepositioned transapical valve replacement with wire-loop repositioning is a viable bailout.

title: Zero-Contrast Transcatheter Aortic Valve-in-Valve Replacement Guided by Continuous Hemodynamic Monitoring.
authors: Mizuki Miura; Yusuke Watanabe; Jo Omiya; Ken Kozuma
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
abstract: An 89-year-old man with structural deterioration of a surgical aortic bioprosthesis and renal dysfunction underwent zero-contrast transcatheter aortic valve-in-surgical valve (TAV-in-SAV) implantation. A SavvyWire provided continuous left ventricular pressure monitoring and rapid pacing during the procedure. After implantation of a 23-mm self-expanding valve, a residual transvalvular gradient was detected, prompting balloon postdilatation under rapid pacing. Repeat invasive hemodynamic assessment showed improvement, and echocardiography demonstrated a mean gradient of 12 mmHg. At 12 months, the patient was in New York Heart Association class I, with preserved renal function and a mean gradient of 8 mmHg. Continuous pressure monitoring may support intraprocedural assessment and guide valve optimization when contrast exposure is being avoided in patients with renal dysfunction.

title: Cost-effectiveness of transcatheter aortic valve implantation for asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
authors: Hussain Abdulrahman Al-Omar; Madison Montgomery; Heather Davies; Elana Greaves; Reagan Davis; Lucy Hillcoat; Hazim J Rahbi; Adham Salem; Pascal Candolfi; Abdulaziz Al Rabiah
abstract:
Aortic stenosis (AS) is defined as the narrowing of the aortic valve. The benefits of implementing early aortic valve replacement (AVR), while the AS is asymptomatic, have been demonstrated in various clinical trials compared with clinical surveillance (CS) of delayed AVR upon symptom onset. The study aims to estimate the cost-effectiveness of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) for the treatment of asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (aSAS) in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA).
A cost-utility analysis compared TAVI using the SAPIEN 3/SAPIEN 3 Ultra valve with CS in an aSAS population. A Markov model consisting of three health states-alive and well, stroke, and death-captured the peri-procedural and long-term outcomes across a lifetime horizon. Inputs were derived from the EARLY TAVR trial (NCT03042104) and existing literature.
The model findings estimated that TAVI was cost-saving and more effective (dominant) compared with CS for people with aSAS, with a 97.3% probability of being cost-effective. Incremental results per person included an estimated cost saving of SAR 33,414, an estimated quality-adjusted life year gain of 0.17, and an estimated life-year gain of 0.12. The key driver of the model was the weighting of disabling stroke for the CS arm.
Early implementation of TAVI for those with aSAS is estimated to result in reduced costs and greater benefits compared with CS. These findings support the idea that timely intervention could enhance AS disease management in line with KSA policy.

title: Metformin Reduces Vascular Inflammation as Assessed by PET in a Mouse Model of Early Atherosclerosis.
authors: Jingjin Hou; Yiming Li; Ning Zhao; Qingbin Hou; Hao Yu; Jiaxin Xu; Jiaqi Zhang; Haixu Song; Chenghui Yan
abstract: Background: Atherosclerosis is the principal pathological substrate of cardiovascular events. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) can assess inflammatory activity within plaques. It is unclear whether metformin acts mainly on early atherosclerotic plaque development or on existing lesion burden to stabilize vulnerable plaques. Moreover, longitudinal imaging to evaluate the stage-dependent antiatherosclerotic effects of metformin warrants further study. Methods: ApoE-/- mice were fed a Western diet for 20 weeks to induce atherosclerosis. In vivo and ex vivo 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging were used to longitudinally quantify 18F-FDG uptake in various aortic segments at 8, 12, and 20 weeks. Additionally, the study evaluated the effects of metformin at two dose levels (low: 250 mg/kg/d; high: 500 mg/kg/d) on plaque burden and inflammatory uptake at early and advanced atherosclerotic stages. Results: Aortic 18F-FDG uptake measured by PET/CT was associated with plaque burden and selected vulnerability-related pathological features. 18F-FDG uptake, quantified as both the average standardized uptake value (SUVmean) and the maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax), was significantly positively correlated with plaque areas in the abdominal and thoracic aorta. Higher 18F-FDG uptake in the aortic arch was associated with greater plaque burden, more severe luminal stenosis, and increased macrophage-associated MMP13 and SSTR2 staining in aortic root sections. During early atherogenesis, metformin reduced vascular 18F-FDG uptake and plaque area, decreased necrotic core and fibrotic areas within plaques, and lowered serum total cholesterol and triglyceride levels. These changes were accompanied by increased aortic AMPKα phosphorylation. In aged ApoE-/- mice with advanced atherosclerosis, low-dose metformin reduced abdominal aortic SUVmean without significant changes in SUVmax or the mean target-to-background ratio (TBRmean). Neither dose significantly reduced 18F-FDG uptake in the thoracic aorta, ascending aorta, or aortic arch. Conclusions: Our findings support the potential value of 18F-FDG PET/CT for noninvasive assessment of disease activity and monitoring of treatment response in murine atherosclerosis. Metformin attenuated vascular inflammation and plaque formation during early atherogenesis, and these changes were associated with increased aortic AMPKα phosphorylation. In the advanced-stage model, treatment-associated reductions in vascular 18F-FDG uptake were not consistently detected. These findings suggest that the vascular effects of metformin may vary with disease stage.

abstract: Introduction: Height, weight, and age of person has significant impact on the normal size of heart. These parameters need to be considered when cut-off values indicating the need for treatment or even surgery are established. The aim of present work is to study the relation of weight of the heart with age and weight of cadaver. Material and Methods: The study was performed in the Department of Anatomy, Shri Ram Murti Smarak Institute of Medical Sciences, Bareilly on 30 hearts from embalmed cadavers. The hearts were procured from the cadavers available in our department. The heart was thoroughly cleaned and measurements were taken. Results: The mean heart weight was 223.37 ± 57.78 g. title: Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
authors: Katane Elizabeth Kekana; Thokozani Isaac Mtshali
journal: Journal of Education and Learning Technology
abstract: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
authors: Muhammad Nur Hudha; Riezky Maya Probosari; Annisa Nur Khasanah; Supurwoko; Salsabila Kholifahtun Nisa’; Gifran Rihla Gifarka Latief
journal: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored. Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement. Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization. Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
authors: Dr. Sunita Dixit
journal: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)
abstract: The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.

journal: Научный журнал "Вестник Актюбинского регионального университета имени К. Жубанова"
abstract: In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.

title: Forward Stroke Volume and Ejection Fraction Estimation in Mitral Regurgitation: A Computational Hemodynamic Approach
authors: Amirahmad Saeidi; Mobina Ghajar; Sara Tarkiani; Amin Ramezani
abstract: Mitral regurgitation (MR) is a common valvular heart disease in which con- ventional measures such as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) can be misleading, as they do not distinguish between effective forward flow and regurgitant volume. This limitation may result in underestimation of the true hemodynamic burden of the disease. In this study, we develop a computational framework based on a closed-loop lumped-parameter cardiovascular model to evaluate forward cardiac function in MR. The model incorporates a regurgitant pathway across the mitral valve together with flow calculations at the left ventric- ular outflow tract (LVOT), allowing estimation of forward stroke volume (FSV) and forward ejection fraction (FEF).The model was first assessed against published physiological reference values and then used to simulate different levels of mitral leakage. As simulated regurgitant fraction increased from 0% to 58.30%, FSV decreased from 65.35 to 51.37 mL and FEF from 60.22% to 35.21%, while LVEF increased from 60.17% to 84.40%. These results illustrate how increased LVEF can coexist with reduced forward output in modeled MR. Overall, the proposed approach provides a physiologically interpretable and computationally efficient tool for analyzing MR hemodynamics. The framework provides a research tool for investigating MR hemodynamics and compar- ing conventional and forward-flow-based measures. Further validation using patient-specific clinical data is required before it can be considered for clinical application.

title: Cellular and molecular mechanisms of arrhythmogenesis in Takotsubo syndrome (Review)
authors: Danqi Xu; Xuan Chen; Maolin Hao; XU Qianqian; Binbin Zhao; Wenjun Huang; Xiaobo Zhou; Qiang Xu; Huan Lan
abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS), an acute stress‑induced heart failure, is frequently complicated by arrhythmias that significantly worsen prognosis. Despite advances in understanding its pathology, the electrophysiological basis of these arrhythmias remains incompletely elucidated. The present review synthesizes current evidence to explore the core electrophysiological mechanisms underlying arrhythmogenesis in TTS, including abnormal calcium handling, repolarization abnormalities, altered conduction and refractoriness due to structural remodelling, and autonomic nervous system imbalance. The corresponding clinical manifestations of ventricular arrhythmias, atrial arrhythmias and bradyarrhythmias were further delineated, and contemporary diagnostic and therapeutic strategies were discussed. By integrating clinical observations with experimental findings, the present review aims to bridge the knowledge gap between mechanistic insights and clinical practice. Finally, critical research gaps were highlighted and future directions were proposed, emphasizing the need for personalized medicine and novel therapeutic targets to improve arrhythmia management and patient outcomes in TTS.

title: Double Jeopardy: Acute Mitral Flail and Culture-Negative Endocarditis in Bicuspid Aortic Valve Stenosis - A Case Report
authors: Maia-Ioana Boureanu; Ileana Grigore; Amalia-Stefana Artenie; Ruxandra Cojocaru; Katherine Mohr
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Introduction Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is the most common congenital cardiac malformation, frequently causing accelerated valvular degeneration and premature aortic stenosis. Although often asymptomatic, incident dyspnea, angina and syncope indicate advanced disease requiring surgery. Sudden severe de novo mitral regurgitation (MR), resulting from structural leaflet abnormalities or functional ventricular impairment, introduces diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, rapidly complicating the clinical course. Case Presentation We analyse the case of a 52-year-old woman with known severe BAV stenosis, ascending aortic aneurysm and prior deferred elective surgery who presented to the emergency department with dyspnea and orthopnea. She recently completed three 7-day empirical antibiotic courses (amoxicillin-clavulanate, levofloxacin, clarithromycin) for a respiratory infection. Upon admission, inflammatory workup showed elevated C-reactive protein (13.3 mg/dL) with normal leukocytes (7,700/mm³) and negative blood cultures. Transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography revealed severe MR caused by posterior mitral leaflet flail (rupture of three chordae at the P2–P3 segments) and a suspected mass on a ruptured chorda, pointing towards infective endocarditis (IE). Cardiac computed tomography showed mitro-aortic curtain thickening with peripheral calcifications and a central high-density area suggestive of an organized thrombus or chronic abscess. Fulfilling major Duke criteria (imaging and direct surgical inspection), intraoperative findings confirmed native aortic valve vegetations and a mitro-aortic curtain abscess, which was evacuated. Surgical intervention consisted of mechanical aortic valve replacement (Bicarbon Slimline), reduction ascending aortoplasty and mitral repair with two neochordae and an incomplete ring. Following a favorable recovery, the patient was discharged in stable condition on acenocoumarol anticoagulation, beta-blocker, diuretic and statin therapy. Conclusion This case illustrates the diagnostic challenges of culture-negative endocarditis masked by prior antibiotic therapy in patients with severe BAV stenosis and acute mitral flail. When blood cultures and imaging alone are inconclusive, intraoperative confirmation remains decisive. Timely multimodal evaluation and combined surgical reconstruction are essential to manage these complex multi-valvular cardiac infections.

title: When Everything Looks Like Amiodarone: Diagnostic Challenges in a Polymorbid Elderly Patient
authors: Maria  Teodora Mitocariu; Carina Maria Ciocan; Sofia Ioana Hanganu; Viviana Ioana Stativa
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Introduction Amiodarone is an efficient antiarrhythmic drug, but can cause cumulative toxicity, including cutaneous, thyroid, pulmonary, hepatic, cardiac and neurological adverse effects. In older patients with multimorbidity and polypharmacy, these effects can mimic existing conditions and complicate diagnosis. Case Presentation A 74-year-old non-smoking woman with persistent atrial fibrillation, treated with electrical cardioversion and maintained on amiodarone for 7 years, presented with exertional dyspnea, palpitations, asthenia, fluctuating blood pressure and vertigo. Amiodarone dose was 200mg/day until September 2026, when it was reduced to 100mg/day, resulting in a cumulative dose of 518g. Patient history included heart failure, moderate mitral regurgitation, hypertension, type IIb hyperlipoproteinemia, osteoporosis, severe coxarthrosis and a recently diagnosed nodular goiter. Telemetry showed resting sinus bradycardia (48-54 beats/minute). She also had progressive sensory polyneuropathy and photodermatitis. The main diagnostic challenge was the intense blue-gray discoloration of the forearms and face, suggesting amiodarone-induced hyperpigmentation. Thyroid-stimulating hormone and thyroid function were normal, and endocrinology review was recommended for the goiter. No skin biopsy was performed. Differential diagnosis ranged from argyria, chrysiasis, ochronosis to heavy-metal deposition, however without compatible exposure. Pigmentation from minocycline, phenothiazines or antimalarials was excluded. Methemoglobinemia was improbable with peripheral oxygen saturation of 98%, and cyanosis from heart failure was excluded by the localized distribution and absence of edema. Amiodarone-induced hyperpigmentation was the leading diagnosis, given the sun-exposed distribution, prolonged treatment and concurrent photodermatitis. Amiodarone was neither stopped nor replaced to preserve sinus rhythm. At discharge, bradycardia persisted and was considered iatrogenic along with neuropathy that improved slowly under gabapentin. Pigmentation persisted, slightly reduced in hospital, probably due to absence of sun exposure. Conclusion Blue-gray skin pigmentation in an older patient on long-term amiodarone requires a structured differential diagnosis, especially with review of medication and exposure history, to avoid premature case closure. Regular monitoring of thyroid function, heart rate, nerves and skin remains essential.

title: When Dyspnea Hides the Heart: A Case Report of Biatrial Appendage Thrombosis and Splenic Infarction Revealing Severe Dilated Cardiomyopathy
authors: Medeea-Andreea Florea; Amalia - Elena Potlog; Ilinca Foia; Sofia-Ioana Hanganu; Radu Amaziliței
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Introduction Heart failure may present with predominantly respiratory manifestations, delaying recognition of underlying cardiac disease. We report severe dilated cardiomyopathy complicated by biatrial appendage thrombosis and systemic embolization. Case Presentation A 52-year-old man with chronic alcohol use and smoking had three hospital presentations within six weeks. The first two (Pulmonology, Infectious Diseases) featured recurrent fever, cough, chest pain, hypoxemia, and bilateral rales, treated as respiratory infections with transient improvement. Four days post-discharge, he presented with confusion, abdominal pain, exertional dyspnea, and dry cough. Evaluation revealed atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, elevated NT-proBNP (7713 pg/mL) and D-dimer, hepatocellular injury, and cholestasis. Transthoracic echocardiography showed biatrial enlargement, LVEF 10%, severe mitral and tricuspid regurgitation, and a dilated inferior vena cava (32 mm). CT pulmonary angiography excluded pulmonary embolism but revealed right (20 × 12 mm) and left (14 × 7 mm) atrial appendage thrombi, with pericardial and bilateral pleural effusions. Abdominal imaging revealed splenic infarction, suggestive of systemic embolization. With low-molecular-weight heparin and guideline-directed heart failure therapy, he improved, with resolving edema and restored sinus rhythm. Repeat echocardiography showed LVEF 15%. He was discharged stable on oral anticoagulation and heart failure therapy. Alcohol-related cardiomyopathy was suspected, although an ischemic etiology had not been excluded; coronary angiography was planned. Conclusion Biatrial appendage thrombosis is uncommon in atrial fibrillation. Symptom overlap, absent cardiac history, and a respiratory diagnostic framework likely delayed echocardiography. This case highlights diagnostic challenges of overlapping respiratory and cardiac manifestations in severe ventricular dysfunction, emphasizing early cardiac assessment in recurrent respiratory presentations. Recurrent fever and splenic infarction raised infective endocarditis as an important differential diagnosis. Although transthoracic echocardiography revealed no visible vegetations, the absence of blood cultures and transesophageal echocardiography precluded its definitive exclusion. Thrombus chronology and causality remain undetermined; long-term outcome is pending.

title: Mitral Valve Prolapse: A Not-So-Innocent Anomaly—Morphological Factors Linked to the Risk of Sudden Cardiac Death
authors: Viviana-Ioana Stativă; Sofia-Ioana Hanganu; Carina-Maria Ciocan; Maria-Teodora Mitocariu
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Introduction Mitral valve prolapse (MVP) affects 2–3% of the global population and is a leading cause of mitral regurgitation in industrialized countries. Although often considered benign, MVP may be associated with ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death (SCD), particularly in young, otherwise low-risk patients. Mitral annular disjunction (MAD) and myocardial fibrosis have emerged as potential markers of an arrhythmogenic phenotype, highlighting the importance of multimodality imaging. Case Presentation We retrospectively evaluated 30 patients with MVP, divided into two groups: 15 patients with MAD and complex ventricular arrhythmias and 15 matched controls with MVP, no MAD, and no ventricular arrhythmias. Mean age was 47 ± 16 years in the MAD group and 49 ± 21 years in the control group. All patients underwent comprehensive cardiological evaluation and multimodality imaging, including cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). In the MAD group, frequent premature ventricular complexes and sustained ventricular tachycardia were documented. Imaging revealed MAD measuring 7–13 mm, predominantly bileaflet prolapse with thickened, redundant leaflets, mitral regurgitation of variable severity and systolic inferolateral wall curling. CMR provided additional tissue characterization, identifying inferolateral late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), suggestive of myocardial fibrosis, in two representative cases. CCTA complemented the assessment through coronary anatomical evaluation. Conversely, the control group exhibited no documented ventricular arrhythmias and no significant MAD. Imaging predominantly showed preserved mitral annular continuity, minimal or absent disjunction, and less pronounced valvular abnormalities. Conclusion Therefore, MVP comprises a heterogeneous clinical and morphological spectrum, with MAD and myocardial fibrosis potentially identifying an arrhythmogenic phenotype. Multimodality imaging, particularly CMR with LGE, enables comprehensive tissue characterisation and refined arrhythmic risk stratification, supporting individualised patient management.

title: Prognostic Value of Right Ventricular–Pulmonary Artery Coupling in Mitral Valve Surgery and Impact of Concomitant Tricuspid Valve Repair
authors: Amila Kahrovic; Harald Herkner; Clemens Gangl; Robert Zilberszac; Iuliana Coti; Alfred A. Kocher; Martin Andreas; Daniel Zimpfer; Paul Werner
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract: Background The prognostic impact of baseline right ventricular‐pulmonary artery coupling on clinical outcomes following mitral valve surgery with specific consideration of concomitant tricuspid valve repair remains uncertain. Methods A total of 214 patients who underwent mitral valve surgery and presented with moderate tricuspid regurgitation at the index procedure were included. Patients were classified after baseline right ventricular‐pulmonary artery coupling (impaired versus normal). The primary study end point was a composite outcome of all‐cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Secondary study end points included all‐cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Results Impaired right ventricular‐pulmonary artery coupling was observed in 112 patients (52%), while 102 patients (48%) had normal right ventricular‐pulmonary artery coupling. The rate of concomitant tricuspid valve repair was similar between study groups (50.0% versus 49.0%, P =0.886). Impaired right ventricular‐pulmonary artery coupling was associated with a higher hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 2.60, 95% CI 1.32–5.14, P =0.006), heart failure hospitalization (adjusted hazard ratio 3.29, 95% CI 1.27–8.54, P =0.014), and all‐cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 2.25, 95% CI 1.11–4.59, P =0.025) during follow‐up. Additionally, concomitant tricuspid valve repair in patients with moderate tricuspid regurgitation was associated with a lower hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 0.45, 95% CI 0.26–0.80, P =0.007). Conclusions Impaired right ventricular‐pulmonary artery coupling is a predictor of adverse outcomes after mitral valve surgery. Concomitant tricuspid valve repair for moderate tricuspid regurgitation seems to be associated with improved outcomes.

title: Can Severe Coronary Artery Disease Fully Explain a Dilated Cardiomyopathy Phenotype? A Case Report
authors: Andreea Simiuc; Anna Maria Iuroaia
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Introduction Dilated cardiomyopathy is characterized by ventricular dilation and impaired systolic function, with a heterogeneous etiology including genetic, toxic, and inflammatory factors. Distinguishing ischemic from non-ischemic myocardial injury can be challenging, particularly when significant coronary artery disease coexists with potential toxic exposure. Case Presentation A 56-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus and compensated toxic cirrhosis presented with exertional dyspnea. He reported consuming approximately 1–2 glasses of wine at each meal over the preceding 15 years, with occasional beer or spirits consumption. Clinical assessment revealed tachycardia, lower-limb edema, diminished breath sounds and bilateral pleural effusions. NT-proBNP (4,874 pg/mL), GGT (504 U/L) and LDL cholesterol were elevated. ECG demonstrated tachycardia, supraventricular and ventricular ectopy and left ventricular hypertrophy. Echocardiography revealed left ventricular dilation, severe global systolic dysfunction (LVEF 24%), diffuse hypokinesia and mild mitral regurgitation. Coronary angiography demonstrated multivessel disease: 50% left main, 75–80% left anterior descending, 90% left circumflex stenosis, and complete right coronary artery occlusion. Preoperative cardiac MRI confirmed left ventricular dilation, severe systolic dysfunction (LVEF 28%) and diffuse hypokinesia. Late gadolinium enhancement showed a mid-wall distribution in the basal interventricular septum, without myocardial edema or ischemic-pattern scarring, providing information relevant to myocardial viability. A 25-gene cardiomyopathy panel was negative, with no relevant family history. Treatment included sacubitril/valsartan, bisoprolol, empagliflozin, furosemide, statin therapy and alcohol abstinence. Holter monitoring detected nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, prompting amiodarone. Surgical revascularization followed. Subsequently, congestion and symptoms resolved, and LVEF improved to 38%. Conclusion Despite severe multivessel coronary artery disease, the absence of ischemic-pattern myocardial scarring on cardiac MRI supported an alcohol-related cardiomyopathy. This case highlights the value of multimodality imaging in differentiating ischemic from non-ischemic myocardial injury. Ventricular functional recovery may reflect both sustained alcohol abstinence and recovery of hibernating myocardium following surgical revascularization, although their individual contributions cannot be distinguished.

title: Wnt MVD study
authors: Na Xu; Katherine Yutzey
abstract: Myxomatous valve disease (MVD) is the most common cause of mitral regurgitation, leading to impaired cardiac function and heart failure. MVD in a mouse model of Marfan syndrome (MFS) includes valve leaflet thickening and progressive valve degeneration. However, the underlying mechanisms by which the disease progresses remain undefined. In this study, we identified Wnt signaling is activated early in myxomatous valve disease progression. Inhibition of Wnt signaling by Dkk1 induction in periostin-expressing valve interstitial cells at 1 month-of-age prevents the initiation of MVD, but late Wnt inhibition starting at 2 months does not prevent MVD progression, suggesting that Wnt signaling contributes to MVD progression in a time-dependent manner and provides a promising therapeutic target for the early treatment of congenital MVD in MFS.

title: Anaesthetic consideration in Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement (TMVR) with LAMPOON procedure in mitral annular calcification: A case report
authors: Namrata Kothari; Maitri Shah
journal: Southeast Asian Journal of Case Report and Review
abstract: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is an emerging treatment for patients with mitral valve disease which includes mitral annular calcification who are deemed high-risk for surgical intervention. However, left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction remains a significant complication. The Laceration of the Anterior Mitral Leaflet to Prevent Outflow Obstruction (LAMPOON) procedure has been developed to mitigate this risk by preemptively splitting the anterior mitral leaflet (AML) before TMVR. The anaesthetic anagement of TMVR remains underrepresented in the anaesthesia literature. Consideration of the procedural approaches, underlying patient pathophysiology, and potential complications allows for the construction of a plan for perioperative management. During lampoon procedure AML laceration causes sudden mitral regurgitation and may cause transient hypotension, wire manipulation increases the risk of arrhythmias and Ballon Inflation & Leaflet Traversal may cause possible transient LV dysfunction. Here, we present the case of a 75-year-old female with severe mitral annular calcification and moderate mitral stenosis with regurgitation, along with severe LV dysfunction. She underwent a successful transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) with a LAMPOON procedure.

title: Lautropia mirabilis-Induced Peritoneal Dialysis-Associated Peritonitis: A Case Report and Literature Review
authors: Shu‐Hui Liu; Yufen Yan; Changcan Hu; Xiuling Huang; Qing Liu; Yanfei Liu; Nan Jia; Chunhua Han
abstract: Background: Lautropia mirabilis is an uncommon Gram-negative facultative anaerobic bacterium primarily colonizing the oral cavity and upper respiratory tract. Peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis (PDAP) caused by this organism is exceedingly rare, with only three previously published cases. Case presentation: We report a 49-year-old woman receiving continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis who presented with cloudy dialysate and abdominal pain. Peritoneal effluent analysis revealed a leukocyte count of 16,522 cells/µL, with 85% polymorphonuclear leukocytes, accompanied by an elevated serum C-reactive protein level of 42.77 mg/L. L. mirabilis was isolated from the dialysate and identified using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry and 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Following intraperitoneal antimicrobial treatment with gentamicin and subsequently ceftazidime, the patient’s symptoms improved. No recurrence of peritonitis was documented during follow-up. A review of the three previously reported cases highlights similarities in clinical presentation but differences in microbiological identification and antimicrobial management. Conclusions: L. mirabilis should be recognized as a potential, albeit rare, cause of PDAP. This case highlights the value of appropriate culture conditions combined with molecular identification for detecting unusual pathogens and emphasizes the importance of integrating microbiological findings with clinical and laboratory responses when guiding treatment.

title: Primary Cardiac Sarcoma with Mitral Valve Invasion Complicated by Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura: A Surgical Dilemma
authors: Ashtyn P. Philipsheck; Tomer Z. Karas; Kevin Accola
abstract: Abstract Background Primary cardiac tumors are rare, comprising approximately 0.3–0.7% of cardiac tumors in autopsy series, and sarcomas are the most common primary cardiac malignancy. Most arise in the right atrium as angiosarcoma; left atrial undifferentiated high-grade sarcoma is distinctly uncommon and carries a poor prognosis with low rates of margin-negative resection. Concurrent immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) introduces a management conflict between hemodynamic urgency and prohibitive bleeding risk for which guidance is limited. Case presentation A 63-year-old retired firefighter who participated in World Trade Center (WTC) rescue and recovery operations presented with decompensated heart failure. Imaging demonstrated a mobile left atrial mass prolapsing through the mitral valve with severe functional mitral stenosis (mean gradient 15 mmHg). Concurrently diagnosed ITP, confirmed by bone marrow biopsy, produced refractory severe thrombocytopenia (nadir platelet count 24×10³/µL) that repeatedly delayed operative intervention while the lesion was considered possibly thrombotic. After intravenous immunoglobulin and platelet transfusion raised the count to 60×10³/µL, urgent left atriotomy with tumor debulking and bioprosthetic mitral valve replacement was performed. Pathology showed a 6.2-cm high-grade spindle cell malignancy with 28 mitoses per 10 high-power fields, MIB-1 index approximately 50%, absent lineage-specific markers, and a positive posterior left atrial margin, consistent with primary undifferentiated cardiac sarcoma. He recovered and received adjuvant gemcitabine–docetaxel, but developed cerebral, osseous, pulmonary, and diffuse intra-abdominal metastases by 5–6 months and died shortly thereafter. Conclusions This case demonstrates how a competing hematologic diagnosis can delay resection of an obstructing cardiac malignancy, and how a microscopically positive margin portends rapid progression in undifferentiated cardiac sarcoma. The temporal relationship between the new ITP and the subsequent tumor diagnosis raises the possibility of a paraneoplastic mechanism, which has been described in roughly a quarter of reported cases of ITP associated with solid tumors as an antecedent finding. The patient's WTC exposure history is documented for completeness; malignancies in this population characteristically present at long latency, but no association between WTC exposure and primary cardiac sarcoma has been established, and attribution is not possible from a single case.

title: Distinct designs, complementary strategies: Tendyne and SAPIEN M3 in transcatheter mitral valve replacement
authors: Zhaoyang Ye; Stephanie Sellers; David J. Meier; Tim Attmann; Xiling Zhang; Thomas Puehler; Nina Pommert; Jacob Voran; Won Kim; G. Warnecke; Derk Frank; Georg Lutter
abstract: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) has emerged as a transcatheter treatment option for selected patients with mitral regurgitation (MR) who are unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter edge-to-edge repair. Among dedicated TMVR devices, the Tendyne and SAPIEN M3 systems are the two clinically approved tech platforms with CE Mark and FDA approval. We comprehensively dissect their distinct design features, procedural characteristics, clinical outcomes, and associated complication profiles. Furthermore, we evaluate their respective patient selection criteria and long-term prognostic implications to facilitate evidence-based clinical decision-making for patients with severe MR. Beyond current metallic prostheses, this review extends to the future horizons of TMVR, specifically highlighting the emerging paradigm of tissue-engineered valvular stents and biodegradable scaffolds as potential solutions to overcome current limitations in prosthetic durability and biocompatibility.

title: ASSESSMENT OF CARDIOVASCULAR AND IMMUNOLOGICAL PARAMETERS IN PREGNANT WOMEN WITH ARTERIAL HYPERTENSION
authors: Tamar Svanidze; M. Jgarkava; Tamar Saralidze
abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy are associated with maternal cardiovascular and immunological alterations. Investigation of macrophage–lymphocyte rosettes (MLR) formation in vitro provides additional information. Purpose: Our purpose was to assess cardiovascular changes and activity of immunocompetent cells in pregnant women with hypertensive disorders and to evaluate their dynamics during treatment. Methods: We observed 90 pregnant women aged 18-45y. Arterial hypertension was detected in 24, among them 4 women had preexisting hypertension, 8 had a gestational arterial hypertension, 12 – preeclampsia without other co-morbidities. All P underwent Ecg, echocardiography(TTE), lab tests and estimation of MLR formation in 72-hour blood leukocyte cultures. In healthy donors amount of MLR equals 37,4 ±2.2%, In the physiological pregnant women (ph P) MLR decreases to 22-30%. Elevated levels of MLR were observed in AH compared to healthy Pregnant. Previous studies showed that MLR in vitro increases significantly in P with stress and premature birth. We divided Pregnant women into 4 groups(gr): I- physiological pregnant P, II- P with preexisting hypertension, III- P with gestational arterial hypertension, IV- P with preeclampsia. Results: In I gr amount of MLR was in normal range for pregnant(18 – 29%), while it was moderately increased in II and III gr (30-40%) and significantly increased in IV gr (45-60%) indicating impending premature birth. Notable, that 3P with preexisting hypertension developed peripartum cardiomyopathy after 36 weeks of pregnancy. According to TTE mild mitral regurgitation was observed in 85% of physiological pregnancies, while 33% of pregnants with AH had mild MR and the rest 67% had moderate MR. Left atrial size was normal in physiological pregnancy, in pregnants with arterial hypertension it was normal or borderline increased, in 3 with preeclampsia it was increased. These 3P revealed PPCM with diastolic dysfunction -impaired relaxation, decreased ejection fraction and markedly increased NT-proBNP. In other P with AH or preeclampsia, EF was preserved. Diastolic dysfunction was observed only in 6 Patients with preeclampsia (50% of PE) including Pregnants with PPCM. After treatment and delivery, normalization of blood pressure, resolution of volume overload, and marked reduction of MLR up to normal range were observed. Conclusions: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy are associated with increased MLR formation, reflecting activation of immunological processes. Reduction of MLR levels in parallel with clinical and hemodynamic stabilization, suggests its potential role as a marker for disease severity and effectiveness of treatment in addition to Echo data. Future studies in this direction is reasonable.

title: Transcatheter Mitral Cerclage Ventriculoplasty: 5-Year Outcomes
authors: Toby Rogers; Adam B. Greenbaum; Vasilis C. Babaliaros; Jason R. Foerst; Jaffar M. Khan; Christopher G. Bruce; Annette M. Stine; Xin Tian; Robert J. Lederman
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter mitral cerclage ventriculoplasty places a circumferential tensioning loop around the base of the left ventricle to reduce mitral annular dimensions and reshape ventricular geometry in patients with functional mitral regurgitation and heart failure. Early experience demonstrated reductions in mitral regurgitation and improvements in heart failure symptoms. METHODS: The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute Division of Intramural Research Transcatheter Mitral Cerclage Ventriculoplasty Early Feasibility Study was an investigator-initiated, prospective, multicenter study. Between 1 and 5 years, vital status, serious adverse events, routine clinical documentation, and site-reported transthoracic echocardiography findings were collected. RESULTS: Nineteen procedures were attempted in 18 participants (63% heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, 37% heart failure with preserved ejection fraction). Median age was 73 years, and 63% were female. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year survival was 57%. One participant underwent left ventricular assist device implantation after 2 years, and 1 participant underwent mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair after 3 years; none underwent heart transplantation. The study was suspended after complete heart block developed in 6 participants, including 4 requiring new cardiac implantable electronic devices. Among participants with available follow-up echocardiography, site-reported imaging demonstrated mitral regurgitation reduction and improved left ventricular ejection fraction through 5 years. Symptomatic improvement was most apparent during the first year and attenuated thereafter. CONCLUSIONS: Cerclage ventriculoplasty was associated with mitral regurgitation reduction and improved ventricular function among participants with available long-term follow-up. Symptomatic benefit was greatest during the first year and diminished thereafter, suggesting that favorable remodeling may not fully offset progression of the underlying cardiomyopathy. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03929913.

title: Introduction to transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention
authors: Lisa Serafini; Alessandra Ricci; Roberta Rosati; Marco Metra; Marianna Adamo
abstract: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) has historically been an undertreated valvular disease, but its management has evolved rapidly in recent years, particularly with the development of transcatheter tricuspid valve interventions (TTVI). Building on experience from the mitral field, dedicated devices targeting leaflet coaptation, annular remodeling, orthotopic valve replacement, and heterotopic caval implantation have been developed and are now clinically available. Randomized clinical trials, such as TRILUMINATE, Tri.Fr, and TRISCEND II, have demonstrated the feasibility and safety of these approaches, with consistent improvements in symptoms and quality of life. However, effects on hard clinical outcomes remain less clearly defined, partly due to modest sample sizes, heterogeneous populations, and reliance on composite and patient-reported endpoints. Large registries have provided valuable real-world evidence, underscoring—with respect to outcomes—the importance of procedural success and early referral before advanced right ventricular dysfunction occurs. Although optimized guideline-directed medical therapy remains fundamental, its impact on advanced TR is limited. Emerging data suggest a potential synergy between device therapy and medical treatment, as successful intervention may improve hemodynamics and facilitate guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) implementation and decongestion therapies may fecilitate TTVI Ongoing studies and refined trial designs will be crucial to define optimal patient selection, timing, and long-term outcomes in this expanding field.

title: Population-level emulation enables fast Bayesian calibration of cardiac digital twins
authors: Clara E Jones; Felix Plappert; Derek J. Bivona; Johane Bracamonte; Zarif Hossain; Isabella Aleman; Lyna Luu; Kenneth C. Bilchick; Pim J. A. Oomen
abstract: Purpose: Patient-specific cardiac digital twins have the potential to guide individualized therapy, but generating these in a routine clinical workflow remains challenging. This is especially true when the twins must carry quantified uncertainty: Bayesian calibration requires thousands of simulations per patient, and the emulators that reduce this cost are typically trained one patient at a time. We aimed to train a single emulator across a patient cohort, so that a new patient can be calibrated in minutes without new simulations. Methods: We trained a population-level Gaussian process emulator whose inputs included a 12-dimensional latent encoding of the clinical features of each patient, so that a single emulator represents the whole cohort. We compared spending simulation budgets on resampling the real cohort with augmenting the cohort with digital chimeras, synthetic patients interpolated between real patients. Seven parameters of a closed-loop heart and circulation model were calibrated by Markov chain Monte Carlo to ten clinical biomarkers in 26 patients with left bundle branch block, each using an emulator trained without that patient, and the calibrated posteriors were compared against the full simulator. Results: A single emulator, trained without the held-out patient, calibrated the digital twin of each patient in 59.7-63.0 s per patient, versus 15 h with the simulator. Resampling the real cohort was the more efficient training strategy, bringing every output to R2 greater than or equal to 0.9, which augmentation did not achieve for the same simulation budget. For held-out patients, both strategies performed comparably (median leave-one-out normalized root-mean-square error 11.0% vs. 10.7%; p = 0.745), and error rose with distance from the cohort centroid (Spearman rho = +0.406). The calibrated models showed no cohort-wide bias (median standardized residual -0.12 against the clinical targets), and 95% predictive intervals contained 78.5% of targets, with the largest misfit in systolic blood pressure. Conclusion: Removing the need for new simulations for every new patient is a meaningful step toward uncertainty-aware cardiac digital twins that fit within a routine clinical workflow. Because the simulator, surrogate and sampler are interchangeable, the approach used here can be applied to other (cardiac) models and cohorts.
